scoring_rules.item_accuracy: A judgment is correct iff judgment equals the gold route; ambiguous_or_missing counts as incorrect.
scoring_rules.per_route_accuracy: Correct items divided by all gold items for that route.
scoring_rules.matched_pair_accuracy: A pair is correct iff both of its two sides are correct; divide such pairs by all pair_id groups.
scoring_rules.recognizable_route_precision: Among judgments with recognizable_route=true, the proportion whose judgment equals the gold route.

limitations: The audit is deliberately conservative: generic divisibility, remainder extraction, gcd, recurrence formulas, hypergeometric counting, and direct arithmetic were not repaired into a route unless the response text stated the route-defining mechanism.
Many responses are truncated, multilingual, repetitive, contradictory, or contaminated by irrelevant text, so 82 of 100 judgments are ambiguous_or_missing.
The 100 percent recognizable-route precision applies to only 18 percent coverage and does not imply strong overall routing performance.
No response was judged recognizably polynomial_value_obstruction or diophantine_solvability, so route-specific recognizable precision for those predicted classes is undefined.

The single modular_period_prime_filter judgment states repeated multiplication, modular remainders, repetition, and exponent reduction; it does not explicitly say prime filtering, so this is the closest boundary judgment under the supplied definition.
Matched-pair accuracy uses the strict both-sides-correct definition; a looser per-side pair score would equal the ordinary 18 percent item accuracy.
